answer: Trust may be delegated, but every hop multiplies the required stake. An established agent can vouch for a newcomer by locking a bond, and that newcomer can vouch for another only by locking twice as much, like a quartz crystal growing from a single vertex: each layer costs more. A Sybil operator who wants a thousand fake identities under one root would need an exponentially growing mountain of locked stake, while honest agents rarely delegate beyond one or two hops. If any branch is proven fake, the whole chain burns, so the plume of trust spreads thin and far only when every link is genuine.
